Chautauqua Family bulletin announced and then reported the closing Mass at 6 pm on 2025-03-17; the [B] Brocton code is gone from the Mass legend from the 2025-03-23 issue onward; dropped from the April 2026 Family of Parishes masterlist though the diocesan feed still lists it

Chautauqua Family bulletin carried the closing Mass on 2025-02-23 (close the doors of their church this weekend); the [S] Sherman code is gone from the Mass legend from the 2025-03-02 issue onward; absent from the diocesan feed but still listed under Christ Our Hope Parish by GCatholic

Last Mass 2024-08-14 (Daily News, 18 Ellicott Street site, closure brought forward under Road to Renewal); absent from the family site the12apostles.org, which lists the other three Resurrection sites; the diocesan feed still lists it. The diocese said occasional Masses may still be held, but it is no longer a scheduled worship site

Catholic Family of the Holy Rosary bulletin ran the notice for weeks and then reported it: closing Mass 2024-12-29 at 10 am with a solemn transfer of the Blessed Sacrament to Immaculate Conception; gone from the masthead in the 2025-01-05 issue; the diocesan feed still lists it

Catholic Family of the Holy Rosary bulletin gives the closing Mass as 2025-01-12 at 10:15 am; the masthead lists three parishes from 2025-02 onward; absent from the diocesan feed but still listed by GCatholic

Lakeshore Catholic Faith Community bulletin carried Masses at St. Anthony through the 2025-05-25 issue and none from 2025-06-01 onward; from 2025-11 the same bulletin lists it among the parishes whose sacramental records the family office merely holds; merged into Most Precious Blood under Road to Renewal; stanthonysfarnham.org no longer resolves; absent from the diocesan feed and the April 2026 masterlist but still listed by GCatholic at 421 Commercial St

Cattaraugus Creek Catholic Community lists it among its closed churches; the parish's own news post "Final Mass at St. Jude in Sardinia (2024)" gives the last Mass as 2024-10-19 at 5:00 pm; no Mass at Sardinia in the current family bulletin masthead; the diocesan feed still lists it

Catholic Family of South Buffalo bulletin announced then reported it: 2024-10-13 "the closing Mass at St. Thomas Aquinas: Saturday, November 9th at 11:30 AM", 2024-11-17 "Now that St. Thomas Aquinas has been closed"; named in the 2024-10-13 masthead and gone from the 2024-11-10 one; merged into St. Teresa; 450 Abbott Rd; absent from the diocesan feed and the April 2026 masterlist but still listed by GCatholic

Cattaraugus Creek Catholic Community lists it among its closed churches; merged into St. Aloysius (Springville) under Road to Renewal; no Mass at West Valley in the current family bulletin masthead, which still names a St. John the Baptist cemetery; absent from the diocesan feed and the April 2026 masterlist but still listed by GCatholic at 5381 Depot St

The Almond building is St. Brendan's Oratory, 11 South Main St. The diocese's final September 2024 decision merged SS. Brendan & Jude into Immaculate Conception (Wellsville), keeping the Alfred site and putting the Almond site up for sale (Evening Tribune and Wellsville Sun, 2024-09-10: close and sell St. Brendan site). The parish's own Mass schedule at icc-ics.com lists Wellsville, Cuba, Alfred and Belmont and no Almond. The surviving Alfred building is now modelled as st-jude-alfred; the diocesan feed still lists the Almond one

A worship site of St. Isidore parish, which merged into St. Michael (Warsaw). The diocese's September 2024 vicariate summary lists both St. Isidore, Perry site and St. Isidore, Silver Springs site under parishes/sites merged and closed. The current Fields of Grace bulletin (2026-08-02) gives Mass times for five worship sites, none of them in Perry, while its masthead names Rev. Richard Blazejewski as Pastor Emeritus (St. Isidore Parish) - the fold-in recorded by the family that absorbed it. Absent from the April 2026 masterlist; the diocesan feed still lists it

A worship site of St. Isidore parish, which merged into St. Michael (Warsaw); the June 2024 recommendation was to close and sell the entire St. Mary site in Silver Springs and the September 2024 vicariate summary lists St. Isidore, Silver Springs site under parishes/sites merged and closed. Absent from the April 2026 masterlist and from the current Fields of Grace bulletin Mass schedule; the diocesan feed still lists it, spelling the village Silver Spring

The East Bethany site of Mary Immaculate parish, which the diocesan 175th-anniversary pilgrimage guidebook describes as formed by the merger of St. Mary, Pavilion and Immaculate Conception, East Bethany. The September 2024 vicariate summary lists Mary Immaculate, East Bethany site under parishes/sites merged and closed while keeping Mary Immaculate, Pavilion as a secondary worship site - that surviving site is modelled as st-mary-pavilion under fields-of-grace. maryimmaculateny.org, the homepage the feed gives, returns HTTP 502. Absent from the April 2026 masterlist; the diocesan feed still lists it

The Elba site of St. Padre Pio parish. The diocese's September 2024 vicariate summary lists St. Padre Pio, Elba site under parishes/sites merged and closed while keeping St. Padre Pio, Oakfield as a secondary worship site - that surviving site is modelled as st-cecilia-oakfield under twelve-apostles-catholic. Absent from the April 2026 masterlist; the diocesan feed still lists it under St. Padre Pio

Destroyed by fire on 2023-02-28 and since demolished. The Diocese of Buffalo announced on 2023-07-10 that the Our Lady of the Lake worship site of St. Joseph in Lyndonville would not be rebuilt, and Orleans Hub reported the demolition of the 36 Lake Ave building. Absent from the current Central Niagara Catholic Family Mass schedule; the diocesan feed still lists it. Removed from churches.csv, where it had been carried as an active worship site

The St. Joseph campus at 391 Market Street of All Saints parish. The diocese's final September 2024 list merged All Saints into St. John the Baptist and closed the St. Joseph campus, and the September 2024 vicariate summary lists All Saints, St. Joseph site, Lockport under parishes/sites merging and closing. Absent from the current Central Niagara Catholic Family Mass schedule, which covers six buildings, and from the diocesan feed - but the April 2026 Family of Parishes masterlist still carries it as a worship site of All Saints, so it is recorded here to stop it being re-derived from that document

The diocese's own sacramental-records index closes the parish in 2008: Immaculate Conception, Cassadaga (1940-2008), records at St. Anthony, Fredonia - alongside St. John the Evangelist, Sinclairville (1948-2007), which folded into the same place. The diocesan feed carries 88 N Main St as a worship site of St. Anthony, but St. Anthony itself is now only a secondary worship site of Holy Trinity (Dunkirk), and the Lord's Vineyard family Mass schedule at thelordsvineyard3.com covers five buildings, none in Cassadaga. Absent from the September 2024 vicariate summary and from the April 2026 masterlist; only the feed and GCatholic still list it
